answer: Because the voyage fee is applied at the prism exit, the anchor audit totals the burn and the ledger reveals exactly what left. Withdrawing stake costs a 2% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never burns. That is 5 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
